title: ₹36 crore saved: TGSRTC buses now grade how drivers drive

slides.head: ₹36 crore saved: TGSRTC buses now grade how drivers drive
What happened
slides.body: The i-ALERT system in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses saves about 1.98 lakh litres of diesel a month, TGSRTC MD Anil Kumar said.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: It tracks gear use, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and harsh braking, and grades each driver after every shift.

slides.head: Diesel cost saved
slides.body: It cuts about 6,603 litres of diesel a day, roughly 16.9 tonnes of CO2 daily.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: The system runs in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: APSRTC and KSRTC officials have sought details on how the system performs. Ask: Will the system reach older, non-BS-VI buses too?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

₹36 crore saved: TGSRTC buses now grade how drivers drive

TGSRTC says the i-ALERT system in 1,500 BS-VI buses has saved nearly ₹36 crore in diesel, about ₹2 crore a month.

Why it matters: It tracks gear use, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and harsh braking, and grades each driver after every shift.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
